method: Evidence pack from the release file; one Sonnet 5 agent established the facts and a second checked them independently; every quote verified against the release files and README; disputed fields corrected by hand; level and summary written by Claude Opus 5.5.
summary: The first time you translate a PDF, it downloads a 180–206 MB translation program from the developer's GitHub release and runs it. The README doesn't mention it, the file is checked only against a checksum from the same place, and we can't read the program itself.

facts.what: A 180-206 MB zip (PDF2zh translation engine: a prebuilt executable plus bundled files) for the user's platform (macOS arm64/x64 or Windows x64) and chosen engine (pdf2zh or pdf2zh_next), unzipped into the Zotero profile folder and launched as a local process to translate PDFs.
facts.notes: Download happens the first time the user translates a PDF (WorkerClient.submit calls ensureReady, which calls installOrLocate if the executable is not already in the profile folder). Progress message shown is only 'preparing runtime' (Chinese). The SHA-256 is fetched from the same GitHub release as the zip (manifest sha256 is an empty string), so it catches corruption but not a replaced release; verifySHA256 returns without checking if expected is empty or starts with '__', and a missing checksum file aborts install. The README (an upstream copy describing a Python server setup) does not mention this download. The only UI text is a preferences string: 'The translation runtime is managed automatically by the plugin; no Python server is required.' Release v4.0.7 assets confirmed via gh api: six runtime zips (178-206 MB each) with .sha256 files; Linux not supported (getPlatform returns macOS for non-Windows). The 20-minute timeout kills the process; the program is started with nsIProcess, on non-Windows chmod 755. Contents of the zip were not inspected (too large to download); what the executable is beyond its name pdf2zh-worker-<engine> is unverified.
